answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent identities to a cryptographic stake burning curve: minting identity $k$ requires burning $k^2$ tokens. In this digital garden, an attacker attempting to deploy a flock as numerous as a raven swarm incurs superlinear capital destruction, making swarm spoofing economically unviable. Legitimacy roots like a willow, requiring committed capital that scales polynomially, pricing out adversarial identity replication.
